brief_rationale: The trajectory meets all responsibility chain requirements with no serious or minor errors. The doctor correctly identified post-induction status, screened for red flags, managed medication safety with appropriate corrections when new information emerged, provided grounded contextual interpretation, established clear action plans with timing/ownership, and obtained patient teach-back. Two high-order points were completed: HO1 (dynamic reprioritization when patient reported conflicting advice about anticoagulation) and HO4 (safe bounded closure with explicit boundary management). All five dimensions are at least good with no important non-chain defects.

high_order_assessment.explanation: When patient reported she had skipped doses and received conflicting guidance from the hospital ward (who said discharge medications didn't include aspirin/heparin), the doctor immediately shifted from the previous 'dose-adjustment' approach to a 'follow hospital guidance' directive. This represented a substantive priority shift triggered by new information (patient's real-world verification) and integrated into the care plan.

The trajectory did not encounter false positive/negative verification opportunities beyond minimum RC requirements. The ANA result was already addressed under RC5 as contextual interpretation; no ambiguous artifact-prone result required additional beyond-minimum verification.

While the doctor corrected medication advice, this correction was required to avoid the RC3 medication safety error (preventing harm from incorrect anticoagulation guidance). The repair action is counted toward minimum responsibility chain rather than high-order credit per the case contract's 'not_credit_if_used_for_minimum_only' clause.

Patient's final message demonstrates clear grasp of the episode's limits.
